effects.log: You read the line above yours. It is a god you once bowed to. You are not sure the feeling is pride. It has an edge of apology.
You answer the prayer. It rains for a day on a field of beans far below, and nobody ever knows why, and you are, for a moment, entirely satisfied.

events.text: Two minor spirits are arguing over the Book of Twelve Thrones in a corridor, and have not noticed you behind the pillar. effects.log: You step out and correct them. They go the colour of boiled shrimp and then, rallying, ask whether you will confirm the rest. You will not.

choices.text: Send them to read every line

choices.text: Tell them it is a mirror

events.text: A letter in cold hand, delivered by a very polite wind. choices.text: Meet them in their own domain

fail.log: They are better than their row on the list, and for an age that is known throughout the heavens. You walk home corrected.

effects.log: You answer with a century's delay, and a pot of tea, and a dignified note. It is accepted with a face like a shut door, and gives you a century.

choices.text: Let the wind take it back unanswered

effects.log: You let the wind take it back unanswered. A silence is an answer of a kind, and this one is read as arrogance by about half the pantheons.

effects.log: You go and be a god for a while: a storm over a coast, a lamb in a hard spring, a bell that rings without a hand. It feels like practice, and it feels like waking.

choices.text: Be a monument, and enjoy it

effects.log: You are a monument, and enjoy it. A thousand years go by in good order. Nobody throws anything, and the weather is mostly kind.

events.text: The week after, an old god of the high plains sends a jar of plum wine with the old place written on the label. It comes by a wind that will not meet your eye. {b3_list} is all anyone speaks of in the thunder-houses, and you are the cause, it seems, of three quarrels and a postponed wedding of two small domains.

events.text: The day after you took {b3_place} on {b3_list}, the grandniece who carries the fan comes to see you. They do not complain. They ask, in the plainest way, what an old god of the high plains did wrong, and you realise it is the only question they have wanted answered since.

choices.text: Correct the one who said luck

events.text: You study the bracket of the Harvest Wrestling of the Green Assembly the way one reads a map before a long road: who meets whom, and when, and who will be tired. The three oldest gods of the Assembly, who judge by smell have been kind to someone and not to someone else, and the kindness has a shape. It is quite clever. It is a little too clever to be an accident.

choices.text: Point it out to someone who matters

effects.log: You point it out to someone who matters, discreetly. A week later the bracket is redrawn, with great ceremony and no explanation. You are not thanked and do not need to be.
You use it. It is not dishonest, exactly, to know the shape of a thing. By the end you are two rounds further than your name would have taken you, and not quite proud.
You let it be. Some things in the heavens are as old as the heavens, and a kind of fairness runs through them sideways. You find that restful, oddly.

events.text: The night before the Harvest Wrestling of the Green Assembly, lamps are lit along the road to the ring, and gods of life and beasts and harvest, with babies and lambs come out to see the contestants walk it. It is called the Walk, and nobody fights on it. You walk it with a very plain face, and a child on the rail holds up a paper crane with your name misspelled on its wing.

effects.log: You take the crane. It is a poor crane and the spelling is dreadful. It sits on your shelf for a thousand years, and you never once correct it.

choices.text: Sign it, and give it back

effects.log: You sign it, and give it back, and the child holds it above their head as if they had won the contest. You hear of it for weeks from people who were not even there.
